Everyone walks through the same door to get here.

Welcome.

A transmission from a Void relay was intercepted. The operator used a 4-byte
keyword cipher — each plaintext byte is shifted by the corresponding key byte
 (mod 256). We know the ciphertext. Can you recover the message

challenges.title: Signal Loss
challenges.description:
A short radio transmission was intercepted before the signal abruptly
disappeared. Analysts believe the message has been encoded in multiple layers to
conceal its true contents.
Recover the original message.
Flag Format: 0xV0ID{...}

> https://files.onebytectf.online/onebytectf/Crypto/secret.wav

challenges.title: V01D Handout
challenges.description:
We pulled node V-7 out of the water three days ago. The board was potted,
the key file was shredded, and the only thing still readable was one
outbound drop and the tool that sealed it.

Three seals. Whoever built this was proud of it — they left the whole
machine in plain sight and kept nothing back but the key material.
That is either arrogance or an invitation.

Unwrap it in order. Each seal is the key to the next one.

challenges.title: Midnight Trace - 1
challenges.description:
Identify the external IP, affected host, and first payload that started the intrusion chain.
Submit format example: 0xV01D{ip_HOST_payload}

challenges.title: Two Sides of Midnight
challenges.description:
**Difficulty:** Expert  
**Expected solve time:** 2–4 hours

A mysterious inline device failed just after midnight. Two synchronized capture points surrounded it and were merged into one PCAPNG. Logs say the device modified one binary upload without changing TCP sequence space while other uploads continued in the background.

Identify the changed flow, recover the evidence that exists on neither side alone, and extract the flag.

Keep PCAPNG interface identity. A duplicated packet is not necessarily an identical copy. No brute force or external service is required.

Flag format: `0xV01D{...}`

challenges.title: Echoes in the WAL
challenges.description:
**Difficulty:** Expert  
**Expected solve time:** 2–4 hours

At 21:03 a field phone received a notification confirming an encrypted attachment was ready. Seconds later the attachment was replaced and a remote deletion policy ran. The current database says everything is gone, but the evidence collector captured the app files while it was active.

Recover the attachment that was valid **at the exact notification time**, then extract the flag.

- Preserve the originals; some SQLite tools change directory state when opened.
- The phone timezone is documented in the package.
- No password guessing or brute force is required.
- Every fact required to decrypt the attachment is inside the evidence set.

Flag format: `0xV01D{...}`

challenges.title: BlackOut - 1
NULLSTAR // BREACH
challenges.description:
At 02:11 local, the IDS on the NULLSTAR perimeter threw one alert and then
nothing. By the time anyone looked, a box was already talking to the outside
on its own.

You have a single capture from the victim's segment — capture.pcap. Everything
the intruder did to that host is in there, from the first knock to the last
thing they smuggled out. Walk it end to end.

Eight answers. They get harder. The last one didn't leave by any door you'd
think to watch.
__
Flag for this stage is 0xV01D{1_R34D3D_7H3_D35CR1P710N}

challenges.title: A Simple Spectrum
challenges.description:
We intercepted this audio file from a deep-space relay station. It sounds like static to our analysts — but our algorithms detected anomalous frequency patterns. Maybe the flag isn't something you hear... it's something you see.

Flagformat : 0xV0ID{}

challenges.title: Acrostic
challenges.description:
FINAL SUBMISSION WARNING
This challenge allows only 1 flag attempt. Submit only when you are sure.
A mysterious message was intercepted from the network. Something is hidden in plain sight. Read carefully — the first letter of each line reveals the secret. Flag format : 0xV0ID{......}

challenges.title: Between The Lines
challenges.description:
An old poet left this manuscript on a dead drop server. Our forensic team says it looks like a normal poem. But something feels off about the spacing. Read carefully — not the words, but the gaps between them.
Flagformt : 0xV0ID

challenges.title: Quiet Note
challenges.description:
FINAL SUBMISSION WARNING
This challenge allows only 1 flag attempt. Submit only when you are sure.
A small artifact is provided. Inspect it carefully and recover the single valid flag. Flag format : 0xV01D{......} Submit the complete flag exactly as shown by the format, including the prefix 0xV01D and the braces.

challenges.title: Single Byte
challenges.description:
FINAL SUBMISSION WARNING
This challenge allows only 2 flag attempt. Submit only when you are sure.
A binary blob was extracted from RAM. It's not plaintext — but it's close. Single-byte operations are often reversible. Try all 256 possibilities. Flag format : 0xV0ID{......}

challenges.title: Time Machine
challenges.description:
An old container image has been recovered from an unknown source. The contents may reveal more than expected. Explore carefully and uncover the hidden secret.

```bash
docker pull jinx69/timemachine:latest
```

challenges.title: LosIlluminados.apk
challenges.description:
Our threat intel team pulled this APK off a decommissioned internal
notification pipeline before the server was wiped.

The developer left a signal bundle inside — supposedly encrypted.
The receiver logic is still intact. Multiple decoy flags are buried
in the app to waste your time.

Reverse the interceptor, figure out how the key is derived,
and decrypt the signal.

Flag format: 0xV0ID{...}

challenges.title: PingBack.apk
challenges.description:
A network monitoring app ships with an exported `BroadcastReceiver` that was meant for internal device diagnostics. The receiver listens for a custom action, validates an auth token and a sequence number, then decrypts and logs an internal unlock signal.

The developers never removed it from the release build. The receiver is listening. Send the right Intent and check the logs.

challenges.title: Nahar Splits
challenges.description: An MDM export contains a base package and split companions from the same device. Treat the set as one artifact; partial views are unreliable.

challenges.title: 0b51d14n_k3y
challenges.description: We receive `obsidian_key.zip`. The description says a cleanup script never finished after a failed migration — implying leftover development artifacts are hiding inside the build. The goal is to recover an AES-GCM-encrypted secret from an Android APK by assembling a key from native library fragments.

challenges.title: Mawj Relay
challenges.description: A small Android package was pulled from an incident response phone. Its notification flow records more than the UI admits. The archive is self-contained.

challenges.title: VoidNotes.apk
challenges.description:
Our threat intel team recovered this note-taking app from a
compromised employee device. The developer insists the notes
are "encrypted" and completely safe from prying eyes.

We're not so sure. Can you recover the secret developer note?
Flag format: 0xV0ID{...}

challenges.title: Concert?
challenges.description:
A friend sent me this screenshot from an old concert and said...:

 there was an interesting story behind it.
 Can you figure out which band it is, where and when the concert took place, what time it started, and who recorded it?
 
Flag Format: 0xV01D{Band-Name_Concert-location_Camera-man-name_begin-time}

challenges.title: Blue Anchor Imports
challenges.description:
An anonymous tip claims that Blue Anchor Imports, a specialty foods importer, is actually a front for laundering money through international shipping containers.

Investigators managed to obtain a single photograph of a container believed to be involved in the operation. No other evidence is available.

Follow the digital trail, unravel the network behind the company, and identify the real person running the operation.
> Flag Format: 0xV01D{full_name}

challenges.title: Ground Below
challenges.description:
The photograph below was taken during the construction of a real, publicly documented site. No readable sign, EXIF metadata, or obvious landmark has been provided.

Your task is to identify the exact facility shown or represented by the construction scene and determine the country in which it is located. A broad answer such as a city, region, or nearby refinery is not sufficient.

Submit the flag in the following format:
0xV01D{<facility-name>_<country>}
	
	---
	
Example:
0xV01D{new_haven_terminal_atlantis}

challenges.title: Sunset Cruise
Basalt Below
challenges.description:
The image below was taken inside a real natural feature somewhere in the  Peninsula. It contains no readable sign, visible landmark, or intentionally provided metadata.

Identify the exact cave, the volcanic field in which it is located, and the country. A broad answer such as a mountain range, province, or nearby city is not sufficient.

Submit the flag in this format:

0xV01D{cave_name_volcanic_field_country}



Normalize the answer to lowercase ASCII letters and underscores. Remove punctuation, apostrophes, hyphens, and articles. For this challenge, use the canonical English transliteration defined by the challenge Author : rdqva

challenges.title: Blue Cabin, Orange Trail
challenges.description:
You are given a single de-metadataed image captured from inside an airport coach somewhere in East Asia.

The route is not directly readable from the challenge image alone. To solve it, identify the country, narrow down the operator, pivot into publicly posted companion photos tied to the same ride, and confirm the exact vehicle.

Recover the English destination shown on the matched bus, the printed vehicle identifier, and the two visible seat labels above the row nearest the photographed passengers.

Flag format: 0xV01D{destination_vehicleid_leftseat_rightseat}

challenges.title: Find Me
challenges.description:
A single street photo. No caption, no coordinates, no metadata. Somewhere in the world, this exact road exists , find it.
 
FLAG FORMAT: 0xV01D{Locality-City-Country}

challenges.title: Map Detective
challenges.description:
Look closely at the maritime views. Find the coordinates.

**Flag format:** `0xV01D{xx.xxx,xx.xxx}`

challenges.title: The Zodiac Archive
challenges.description:
A private collector claims to possess four original letters attributed to the Zodiac Killer. Although all four appear authentic, investigators believe one contains a historical inconsistency. Examine the scans, verify the historical details using publicly available sources, and identify the forged document
Flagformat : 0xV0ID{YEAR_NAME}

challenges.title: The Elephant in the Archive
challenges.description:
**Difficulty:** Medium / Hard  
**Expected solve time:** 1–3 hours

In 1896, a building that barely looked like a building disappeared. One of its relatives still survives, while modern sources disagree about the numbers and dates behind its story.

Use `evidence.png` to identify the lost building, then recover these values in order:

1. The six-digit US patent number for the animal-shaped building idea.
2. The exact one-word room label in the 1887 tourist guide—the room from which the elephant was fed. Preserve the printed spelling.
3. The number of **full working days** required to construct it according to that 1887 guide.
4. The public school number currently near the historical site, normalized as `psNN`.
5. The fire date itself as `YYYYMMDD`, not the next day's newspaper date.

Flag: `0xV01D{patent_room_days_school_yyyymmdd}`. Public sources only; no accounts, payment, contact, or scanning is required.

challenges.title: q3 — The Vault
challenges.description:
# q3 — The Vault (pwn)

| | |
|---|---|
| Port | 20003 |
| Points (suggested) | 400 |
| Files | `chall`, `libc.so.6` |
| Difficulty | Very Hard |

**EN:** Every mitigation is on: canary, PIE, full RELRO, NX. One careless
`printf(buf)` gives you a single format-string round. Use it to carve out
the canary, the PIE, and the libc from the stack — then one more gift
overflows into a ROP chain. The vault opens from the inside.

`nc 35.192.106.100 20003`

**AR:** كل الحمايات مفعلة: canary، PIE، Full RELRO، NX. `printf(buf)` وحدة
متهورة تعطيك جولة format string واحدة. استخدمها لتقتطع الـ canary والـ PIE
والـ libc من الـ stack — وبعدها هدية ثانية تفيض وتزرع ROP chain. الخزنة
بتفتح من جوّا.

## Files
- `chall` — 64-bit ELF (NX, PIE, canary, FULL RELRO)
- `libc.so.6` — glibc 2.39 (the exact one on the server)

challenges.title: q2 — RopCSU
challenges.description:
# q2 — RopCSU (pwn)

| | |
|---|---|
| Port | 20002 |
| Points (suggested) | 250 |
| Files | `chall`, `libc.so.6` |
| Difficulty | Hard |

**EN:** No `win()`. No leaks. The binary only offers `puts` and `read`.
The libc is in your hands — you just have to find it at runtime. The
`__libc_csu_init` gadgets are waiting to call anything you point them at.
Two-stage: leak, then land.

`nc 35.192.106.100 20002`

**AR:** ما في `win()`. ما في أي تسريب. الباينري ما يعطيك غير `puts` و `read`.
الـ libc بين إيديك — بس لازم تلقاه وقت التشغيل. كيدجيتات `__libc_csu_init`
مستنية أي شي توجّهها له. مرحلتين: تسريب، ثم إصابة.

## Files
- `chall` — 64-bit ELF (NX, no PIE, no canary)
- `libc.so.6` — glibc 2.39 (the exact one on the server)

challenges.title: q1 — Shellgame
challenges.description:
# q1 — Shellgame (pwn)

| | |
|---|---|
| Port | 20001 |
| Points (suggested) | 100 |
| Files | `chall` |
| Difficulty | Medium |

**EN:** The gatekeeper of V0ID only opens for a very specific pair of gifts:
`0xdeadbeef` and `0xcafebabe`. Overflow the guard's stack and hand them over
in exactly the right order. There is a `win()` that will drop you a shell —
but it needs arguments.

`nc 35.192.106.100 20001`

**AR:** حارس البوابة ما بيفتح إلا بهدية محددة: `0xdeadbeef` و `0xcafebabe`.
افعل الفيضان على الـ stack وسلمه الهدايا بالترتيب الصحيح — في دالة `win()`
بتعطيك شيل، بس محتاجة وسائط.

## Files
- `chall` — 64-bit ELF (NX, no PIE, no canary)

challenges.title: TURING'S CURSE
challenges.description:
If you gaze long into the void, the void gazes back.

Inside this binary sleeps a single true name. Speak it, and the core unseals.

But the void is generous with lies. It has carved a hundred false names into its walls, and it whispers easy answers to anyone impatient enough to listen. There are no shortcuts here — no string that saves you, no brute force that outlives the dark. The only way out is to understand exactly how the void transforms what you feed it, and walk that path backwards.

Many will find a flag. Almost all of them will be wrong.

Rule: reverse it properly. The obvious answer is never the answer.

challenges.title: Afterimage Protocol
challenges.description:
**Difficulty:** Expert  
**Platform:** Linux x86-64

The recovery team found one executable still running inside a dead relay. It does not store an identifier, and it does not search for one. It remembers only an afterimage and a path through a folded instruction tape.

Recover the unique identifier accepted by `afterimage`.

Flag format: `0xV01D{[A-Za-z0-9]{16}}`. The body is case-sensitive. No brute force, external service, or Internet access is required.

challenges.title: ChronoCore
challenges.description:
# ChronoCore

Author: `0x4sh`

A damaged probe came back from the dark side of V0ID with one tiny validator
still alive. It does not store the answer, and the obvious strings are only a
door frame. Recover the state machine, understand how time is shuffled, and
walk the core backwards.

File: `chronocore`

challenges.title: Transmission

challenges.title: Palimpsest Vault
challenges.description:
The vault signs viewing tickets for public folios. The clerk says it checks the shelf path before stamping the ticket. The renderer says old ink needs more patience than that.

Recover the uncatalogued folio.

challenges.title: Loopback Lens

# Loopback Lens

Author: `0x4sh`

The public lens can fetch pages for you, but its private calibration route is
supposed to exist only from inside the machine. The guard checks the obvious
faces of localhost. Give it a less obvious mirror.

URL: http://35.192.106.100:21001/

challenges.title: Directive

# Directive

Author: `0x4sh`

The card previewer is paranoid about the loud parts of templates. The quiet

URL: http://35.192.106.100:21002/
